note: Promotion to the tracked schema (roadmap Phase 1 backfill). Track groups follow the (XX) prefixes already embedded in the source theme names; only empty fields are filled.

tracks.name: The daily care of a body

themes.description: The two-minute method that reaches every surface — angle, motion and the places every mouth misses.

themes.theme: Why the toothbrush matters more than the toothpaste (DC)
themes.description: Bristles, replacement and technique as the working parts of oral care, with paste as the assistant.

themes.theme: The tooth that hurts is already late (DC)
themes.description: The decay timeline — white spot, cavity, ache — and the stages where it can still be stopped.
The full handwash and the four moments that actually transmit illness — before food, after the toilet, after care, after coming in.
Your own household's water path from source to cup, and the points where it can be protected or contaminated.

themes.theme: The nail, the cut, the scrape (DC)
themes.description: Cleaning, dressing and watching a small wound — and the redness, heat and swelling that mean infection.
What sleep does for a body and mind, how much each age needs, and the habits that protect it.
Protecting a body from your own climate — shade, water, layers — and reading heat exhaustion and hypothermia early.

themes.theme: Shoes, feet and standing all day (DC)
themes.description: Foot care for people who work on their feet — fit, hygiene, and the small problems that disable when ignored.

themes.theme: Keeping a body clean without much water (DC)
themes.description: Staying genuinely clean on a few litres — the priority areas, the method and the dignity of managing it.

themes.theme: What a tooth is made of (MO)
themes.description: Enamel, dentine and pulp — the layers of a tooth and what each one can and cannot repair.

themes.theme: Sugar and time, not sugar alone (MO)
themes.description: Why frequency of sugar exposure decays teeth faster than quantity, and what that changes about snacks and drinks.
Healthy versus inflamed gums, the plaque line that causes the difference, and reversing early gum disease.
The eruption order of the adult teeth and the six-year molar that is so often mistaken for a baby tooth.
What fluoride does to enamel, where it comes from, and the evidence stated plainly enough to repeat.

themes.theme: The dental visit nobody has had (MO)
themes.description: What actually happens in a dental check-up, step by step, for someone who has never been.
The dental emergencies — swelling, fever, a face changing shape — and how urgently each must be seen.
The knocked-out or broken tooth — correct handling, storage in milk or saliva, and the clock that decides if it survives.
What smoking and chewing do to gums and tissue, and the visible changes that need a clinician's eye.
Assisted brushing for a child, an elder or a patient — positioning, gentleness and doing it every day.

tracks.name: Eyes and ears in a classroom and a life

themes.theme: The child who sits at the front (EE)
themes.description: The classroom signs of unseen vision problems — squinting, copying, avoiding the board — and what to do about them.
What a screening can and cannot say, and why a failed screen is a referral, not a verdict.
The gap between prescription and wearing — cost, teasing, loss — and the local paths that close it.
Hearing loss mistaken for defiance — the behaviour pattern that should trigger a hearing referral instead of discipline.
The volumes and durations that permanently damage hearing, and the protection that actually gets worn.
Ear infections and swimmer's ear — the signs that pass at home and the signs that need a clinician.
Lighting, distance and breaks — the reading conditions that tire eyes and the cheap changes that fix them.
The correct first response to a struck, cut or splashed eye — and the instinctive responses that make it worse.

themes.theme: Living with a sense that works differently (EE)
themes.description: Practical adjustments for low vision or hearing — seating, light, phrasing — that a household can make tomorrow.

themes.theme: Explaining a referral to a family (EE)
themes.description: Delivering a screening result to a family clearly and kindly — what was found, what it means, what happens next.

tracks.name: Food and water that keep you well

themes.theme: What a body is doing with food (FW)
themes.description: Energy, building and protection — the three jobs food does, and the foods that serve each.
One complete meal cooked safely from start to plate — heat, timing, hygiene and serving.
Storage that extends food — cool, dry, sealed, rotated — matched to what your household actually keeps.

themes.theme: Reading what is on the packet (FW)
themes.description: Dates, ingredients and per-portion numbers — extracting the three facts that matter from any label.
How dirty water makes people ill, the diarrhoea danger to small children, and rehydration done correctly.
The cheap foods that still build a body, and stretching a food budget without losing the protein.
What small children need at each stage, the foods that endanger them, and patience at the plate.

themes.theme: The kitchen that makes people ill (FW)
themes.description: Cross-contamination, temperature and the cloth that spreads — the kitchen habits behind most food poisoning.
One food plant from planting to plate — soil, water, care and the harvest that teaches the chain.
Cooking for a crowd — the batch sizes, holding temperatures and serving hygiene that keep an event safe.

tracks.name: A body and mind that recover

themes.description: Movement as maintenance — what regular use does for muscles, joints, heart and mood at every age.
The lift that spares the back — feet, knees, load close — and the loads that need two people or a tool.
Getting down to and up from the ground in stages — the ability that predicts independence in later life.
Slow breathing as a tool — the technique, and when it genuinely helps with pain, panic and sleep.
Pauses, days off and the difference between rest and collapse — recovering before the body forces it.

themes.theme: When the mind is the thing that hurts (MR)
themes.description: Recognising low mood, anxiety and overload in yourself, and the first steps that are actually available.
Asking directly, listening without fixing, and connecting a struggling person to real help.
Puberty, ageing and everything between — the changes that are normal and the ones worth a check.
The difference between new pain and persistent pain, what makes chronic pain worse, and pacing that helps.
Building one health habit that survives — small, anchored to a routine, and tracked without punishment.
